## 10. Local effect fingerprint vs global resolution fingerprint

The `effect_color` fingerprint and the `ResolutionFingerprint.cache_identity` are
separate identities with different scopes.

V1.39 verifies that changing an effect color changes both identities while the
identities themselves remain distinct. The local operation therefore remains an
operation-level provenance token; the global fingerprint remains the cache identity
for the complete component resolution.

## 11. Serialization

The cache itself is process-local and is not serialized. The fingerprint is
serializable deterministically through the existing canonicalization boundary.
A canonical JSON round-trip reproduces the same SHA-256 identity.

No cache entry is persisted to PostgreSQL or a file by V1.39.

## 12. Performance contract

The real cache was measured for 0, 1, 2, 4 and 8 color effects. Each case used:

- 30 cold resolutions with a fresh cache;
- one stored result;
- 200 warm cache-hit resolutions.

The warm path still computes `resolution_fingerprint()` because the cache must
prove the current identity before returning an entry. V1.39 does not hide this
cost or claim a zero-cost cache lookup.

## 13. Visual acceptance

The before/after board is generated from actual `resolve_component()` output.
The cached result must preserve:

- effective fill color;
- effective contour color;
- alpha semantics;
- resolution provenance.

Cases cover neutral, very dark, mid-tone, high-light, complementary and partial-
alpha/near-color inputs.

The acceptance criterion is pixel-level visual equivalence of the rendered swatches
plus exact equality of the resolved visual/provenance objects.

## 14. Color-operation boundary

V1.39 introduces:

- no new color space;
- no new RGB transform;
- no HSL/OKLab/XYZ calculation;
- no gamut mapping;
- no compositing operation;
- no change to the established `effect.color.srgb8-interpolation` law.

The cache stores the result of the existing resolver; it does not alter the color
operation.

## 15. Version policy

`ENGINE_VERSION` remains `1.3.8`. `SCHEMA_VERSION` remains `2`.

`RESOLUTION_VERSION` advances:

```text
19 → 20
```

because resolution cache semantics and context fingerprint projection are runtime
resolution semantics. This is not a color-operation version bump.

## 16. Required invariants

1. Same complete fingerprint ⇒ same cache identity.
2. Changed resolution dependency ⇒ different cache identity.
3. Canonically equivalent input effect order ⇒ same identity.
4. Cache hit ⇒ no visual/provenance mutation.
5. Duplicate effect IDs ⇒ fail closed.
6. Relation effect metadata changes ⇒ target identity changes.
7. Consequence effect changes ⇒ target identity changes.
8. Unrelated targeted context effects do not invalidate siblings.
9. No new color operation is introduced by the cache.
10. Cache capacity remains bounded and eviction deterministic.
